transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm in the right place for this... um, I'm here because, well, I guess I just feel like I'm always running hot. Like my motor is just constantly going and I can't quite shut it off? Which, you know, usually isn't a bad thing—it actually helps a lot with my job as a firefighter, being ready to go at a moment's notice. But, um, lately, it's been kind of getting me into a little bit of trouble at the firehouse. Just... minor things, really, but I wanted to get it checked out, if that makes sense? Is that the kind of thing you can help with?
Are these troubles at the firehouse causing you significant stress or problems with your relationships with colleagues?

Well... um, I mean, I love my crew, we're a brotherhood, right? So I don't want to make it sound like we're fighting or anything. But... yeah, I guess it is causing some stress. I'm a little embarrassed to even admit this, honestly, but... they actually pulled me into a, uh, a performance and safety meeting recently. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad firefighter, I really do try my best every single shift. 

It's just... I think it's starting to cost me some trust with the guys. I've been working really hard for a shot at moving into leadership, and now it feels like that's kind of slipping away. The crew just feels like they can't always count on me to track all the details consistently right now. Am I explaining that okay? I just really want to fix it so I don't let them down.
Do you often find yourself having trouble paying attention to details or making careless mistakes?

Well... um, I hate to admit it, but... yeah, I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I always try to do my absolute best, I really do. But... there are times with the paperwork where I mess up. 

Like, I’ll finish up an incident report and hand it in thinking it’s completely solid, you know? Ready to go. And then... well, the captain will have to pull me aside and point out that I put down the wrong unit number, or I missed a time stamp somewhere in the middle. Or I just completely skipped some little check box that actually matters a lot for the safety review. 

It's really embarrassing, honestly. I don't do it on purpose, I just... I don't know how I miss them. It's mostly just little paperwork things like that, though. I mean, everybody makes little typos when they're rushing sometimes, right? Does that sound like what you're asking about?
Do you often act on impulse without thinking things through?

Um... I don't think so? I mean, I wouldn't say I'm impulsive, really. 

I guess... well, in my line of work, you kind of have to make split-second decisions, right? You don't always have time to sit and ponder every angle when an alarm goes off. So I'm used to just jumping into action. But I wouldn't call that acting without thinking, it's more like... being decisive? Being ready. 

I don't know, I try to be really thoughtful about the big things in life. I don't just go off and do crazy stuff on a whim or anything. Is that what you mean? Like making big, reckless choices? Because I really try not to do that. I hope that's the right kind of answer... I just don't really see myself as an impulsive guy.
Do you often feel restless or fidgety when you're not actively engaged in a task?

Well... um, I mean, I try really hard to be respectful when people are talking, especially the brass. But... yeah, I guess I do get a little antsy sometimes. 

It's just, you know, we have these long command meetings, and... sitting still through them, it honestly feels like my body is just revving too high. Like my engine is idling too fast, if that makes sense? I just get this overwhelming urge to stand up, go walk the bay, check the rigs... just do literally anything besides stay planted in that chair. 

I really try to hide it, though! I don't want the chiefs thinking I'm not paying attention or that I don't care about what they're saying, because I do. It's just hard to keep my body quiet when we aren't actively doing something. Is that normal for guys in my line of work? I mean, we're kind of built to be moving, right? I hope that doesn't make me sound disrespectful.
Do you feel restless or fidgety at home or when you're not working, or is it mostly just at the firehouse or during meetings?

Well... um, it's not just at the firehouse, I guess. I mean, I really try to be present at home, I do. My family is everything to me. But... yeah, even on my days off, I have a hard time just... doing quiet stuff with them. 

Like, if we try to sit down and watch a movie or something, I... well, I end up talking a lot, or I just start moving around. I'll get up before I've really been sitting that long, maybe go check the tools in the garage or find some little project to fix. I don't mean to ruin their relaxing time, I just... I want to be helpful, you know? Keeping things maintained around the house. 

I hope my wife doesn't think I'm avoiding her or the kids. I'm really not! It's just hard for me to just sit there and do nothing when there's always something that could be worked on. I mean, it's good to be productive on your days off, right? Does that make sense, or... is that a bad thing?
Are you experiencing any difficulties in your relationships with your family or friends outside of the firehouse?

Um... no, no, not really. I mean, my family is great, and my friends are mostly guys from the department, so we all kind of understand each other. 

I guess... well, sometimes my wife gets a little frustrated if I start a project around the house and don't quite finish it before starting another one, but... that's just normal married stuff, right? We don't really fight about it. I always mean to go back and finish things, and I think she knows that. I try really hard to be a good husband and dad. 

I don't think there's any major problems or anything. I mean, everyone has little bumps here and there, don't they? I hope I'm not painting a bad picture of my marriage, because we're really very happy. Is that... does that answer what you're asking?
Do you feel like you're always 'on the go' and can't relax, even on weekends or during vacations?

Well... yeah, I guess that's kind of it. That's actually the main reason I came in to see you. I just... I feel like I'm always running hot, you know? Like I can't shut the motor off, no matter what day of the week it is or if we're supposed to be on vacation. 

I really try to relax when I'm supposed to, I promise I do! But... it's just hard. And, um... well, to be honest, lately, that whole 'never stopping' thing has been getting me into a little bit of trouble at the firehouse. Nothing major! Just... you know, I guess I can be a bit much when everyone else is trying to have downtime between calls. I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job and staying ready, but I guess it comes off wrong sometimes. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad firefighter or a difficult guy to work with. I really respect my crew. Is it... is it normal to feel like your engine is just stuck in drive like that?
Are your family and friends outside of the firehouse noticing any changes in your behavior or mood lately?

Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, my wife hasn't really said anything about me acting different or being in a bad mood or anything like that. I try really hard to leave any stress at the door when I get home. 

Like I said, my friends are mostly guys from work, so they see me all the time anyway. We don't really talk about feelings or moods or anything... we just kind of hang out. So, no, I haven't noticed anyone outside of work saying anything. I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. I'm not trying to hide anything, I just... I don't think there's been any changes like that. Does that make sense?
Are your symptoms interfering with your ability to complete tasks or achieve your goals outside of work?

Um... well, outside of work, I think I'm doing okay. Like I said, the projects around the house sometimes take a little longer, but I always get to them eventually. I really try to stay on top of things for my family. 

But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest... it's really the work stuff that's the problem right now. I know you asked about outside of work, but... well, I was actually pulled into a performance and safety meeting recently. It wasn't a huge deal, I mean, they just wanted to talk about some things... but they mentioned that I've been having trouble tracking details consistently. 

I really pride myself on being a good firefighter, I swear I do. But I feel like this whole thing is starting to cost me the trust of the guys at the house. I was really hoping to move up into a leadership role soon, but now... I don't know, it feels like that might be slipping away because they don't feel like they can count on me with the little things. 

I'm trying so hard to fix it, I really am. I hope that doesn't make me sound careless. I take my job very seriously. Is it... is it helpful that I'm telling you this? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need to help me.
Do you experience these feelings of restlessness and being 'on the go' at the same level when you're alone compared to when you're with others?

Um... yeah, I think it's pretty much the same whether I'm by myself or with the crew. It's just always there, you know? Like... well, for example, when we have command meetings and I have to sit still for a while... it just feels like my body is revving way too high. 

I try really hard to just sit there and pay attention, I promise I do, but... it's like I have this overwhelming urge to just stand up, walk the bay, check the rigs... honestly, just do anything besides stay planted in that chair. I usually manage to keep it together, though! I don't want to be disruptive or anything. 

I just... I feel like I always need to be doing something productive, you know? I hope that doesn't sound like I'm not taking the meetings seriously. I really do try to focus. Does that make sense? Is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Are you finding it difficult to enjoy or participate in activities you normally like to do outside of work due to feeling restless or always 'on the go'?

Um... well, I really love spending time with my family on my days off, I promise I do. I don't want it to sound like I don't enjoy being with them, because they mean everything to me. 

But... yeah, I guess if I'm being completely honest, the quiet stuff is kind of hard for me. Like, if we're trying to just sit down and watch a movie or play a board game... I have a really hard time just staying there. I usually end up talking too much, or just moving around, or getting up before I've really been sitting very long at all. 

I just get this feeling like I need to be doing something useful, you know? So I'll wander out and start checking my tools in the garage, or just pacing around the house. I always try to come right back, though! I don't mean to ruin their relaxing time, and I really hope my wife doesn't think I'm trying to avoid them. I just get so antsy when things are too quiet. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad husband or dad. I really do try my best to be present for them. Is that... is that what you were asking about? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right examples.
Are you finding that your restlessness and always being 'on the go' is causing problems in your personal relationships or daily activities outside of work?

Um... well, no, I don't think it's really causing any big problems. I mean, my wife is pretty understanding about it all. She knows I just like to stay busy and keep things in good shape around the house. 

I guess sometimes she might get a little frustrated if I'm up and down during a movie, but it's never led to any big fights or anything like that. I always make sure to apologize if I'm being a distraction. And with the kids, I think they actually kind of like that I'm always ready to go do something active, you know? 

I really try to make sure my energy is put to good use so it doesn't bother anyone. I hope that makes sense? I just don't want you to think I'm causing trouble for my family because I can't sit still. I'm doing okay with them, I promise. Is that... does that answer your question?
Are you finding it hard to manage your daily routines and responsibilities outside of work due to your restlessness?

Um... well, my routines are mostly okay, I think. I mean, I really try to stay on top of everything. But, um... I guess if I'm being totally honest, things do slip through the cracks sometimes. Not because I don't care! I really, honestly mean to get it all done. 

It's just... I don't know, I get moving too fast or I'm focused on the next thing, and I'll realize I completely forgot to pay a bill until the late fee hits, or... or I'll forget to call someone back. And sometimes at work, I'll forget to sign off on my training modules or bring the right paperwork for my gear when I come on shift. 

I always fix it as soon as I realize, though! I promise I'm not trying to be irresponsible. I just... my brain just kind of skips over things when I'm bouncing around. I hope that doesn't make me sound like I'm terrible at my job or anything. I really do try to keep it all straight. Does that... is that the kind of thing you mean?
Are you finding it difficult to fulfill your responsibilities or complete tasks outside of work due to your restlessness and inability to relax?

Um... well, at home I really try my best to get all my chores done. I promise I do, and my wife is great about helping me stay on track there. But... I guess if I'm thinking about struggling to finish things, I actually notice it a lot at the firehouse, if it's okay to give a work example? I hope that's alright. 

Like, if someone gives me three or four station tasks to do during a shift... I always start out really strong on the first one. I really want to do a good job and pull my weight. But then... I don't know, I just get pulled into something else, or I get a little antsy and move on to the next thing too soon, and later I'll find the hose inventory or the equipment checklist just sitting there, half-done. 

I always go right back and finish it the second I realize! I don't want you or my captain to think I'm lazy or trying to avoid my duties, because I really do care about my job and my crew. I just... I get sidetracked easily when I'm moving around so much. I really try hard not to let it happen, though. Does that... is that the kind of thing you were looking for? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Are you feeling like your restlessness and inability to relax are significantly affecting your overall quality of life?

Um... well, overall quality of life... I mean, I try to stay really positive, you know? I have a great family and I love being a firefighter. I really do. But... um... 

I guess... I guess if I'm being completely honest, it is starting to get a little stressful. I really hate to admit this, because I want to be a good team player, but... my captain actually pulled me into a performance and safety meeting recently. It wasn't... I mean, it wasn't a disciplinary thing, really! They just wanted to check in. 

But it's... it's starting to cost me some trust with the guys at the house. And that really hurts, because I respect them so much. I've been hoping to move up into leadership, and I've been working really hard for it, I promise. But right now, I feel like that chance is kind of slipping away. They just... they feel like they can't count on me to track all the little details consistently because I'm always bouncing from one thing to the next. 

I'm trying so hard to fix it, though! I don't want anyone to think I'm unsafe or unreliable. I just... I really want to do a good job and make my crew proud. I hope it doesn't sound like I'm making excuses. Does that... does that answer your question about how it's affecting things? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
How long have you been feeling like you're always 'on the go' and can't relax?

Um... well, it hasn't always been this bad! I mean, I've always had a lot of energy, which is usually a good thing in my line of work, right? But... as far as it being a real problem where I just can't settle down... 

I'd say it's been about a year and five months? Give or take? That's when we started doing these longer rotating shifts, and they added all this extra documentation we have to do. Oh, and I got assigned drone duties, too! Which is really cool, I was so excited they trusted me with it. But it's just... it's a lot more on my plate all at once. 

Since then, it just feels like my motor is always running, even when I'm off shift. I try really hard to wind down, I swear I do. I don't want to be bouncing off the walls at home or making my crew crazy. I just... it's been harder lately to find that off switch since the schedule changed. Is that... does that timeline make sense for what you're asking? I hope I'm explaining it okay.
Are you feeling like your restlessness is affecting your relationships with your family or friends in a significant way?

Um... well, my wife and kids are so great, they really are. They're super patient with me. But... um... I guess it does affect things a little bit at home, even on my days off. I try really hard to be present and just hang out with them, I promise I do! 

But... if we're trying to do something quiet, like watch a movie or play a board game, I just... I have a really hard time just sitting there. I don't mean to be disruptive, but I'll start talking a lot, or I'll just feel this need to get up and move around. Like, I'll suddenly remember I need to check some tools in the garage, or I'll just pop up from the couch before I've even been sitting there very long. 

I always try to come right back! I don't want them to think I don't want to spend time with them, because I really do. It's just hard for me to do the quiet, sitting-still stuff without getting kind of antsy. I hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad dad or husband. I really do try to focus on them. Is that... is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right picture of how things are at home.
Have you been experiencing these feelings of restlessness and being 'on the go' for more than six months?

Um... yeah, definitely more than six months. Like I mentioned a minute ago, I'd say it's been a real issue for about a year and five months? 

I really don't want it to sound like I'm complaining about work, because I love my job, but... yeah, it really ramped up when they started those longer rotating shifts. And then they added all that extra documentation we have to do, plus assigning me the drone duties. Which, again, I'm super grateful they trust me with! It's just... that's when the feeling of my motor constantly running really started to become a problem. 

I've been trying so hard to get a handle on it since then, I promise. I don't want to let anyone down. Does that... does that answer your question about the timeline? I hope it's okay that I brought up the work stuff again, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.

Are you finding that your difficulties with restlessness and being 'on the go' are significantly impacting your ability to perform your job as a firefighter or affecting your relationships with your crew?

Um... gosh. I mean, my crew is like family, they really are. And I always want to pull my weight, you know? I try so hard to be the guy they can rely on, and I really do care about doing a good job. 

But... well... I guess I should just be completely honest with you. It's... it's actually been getting kind of bad at the station. I didn't really want to bring it up because it's pretty embarrassing, and I don't want you to think I'm a bad firefighter, but... I actually got pulled into a performance and safety meeting recently. 

It just kills me to admit it, but this whole thing has started costing me trust at the firehouse. With my motor always running and having a hard time settling, I've been missing things. The guys... they feel like they can't count on me to track all the details consistently right now. And, um, I was really hoping to move up into a leadership role soon, but now it feels like that shot is just slipping away. 

I'm trying so, so hard to get back on track and fix it, I swear I am. I never want to be a liability to my team. Is that... I hope that's the kind of information you needed? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions right, even if it's a little hard for me to talk about.
